name: service-events
title: Events
description: Cookieless analytics and transactional server audit events built on OTLP, with inherited actor context, trusted geography and event-derived visits.
docs:
## Setup

Cookieless browser analytics, consent controls and server audit events over OTLP. SQL storage is optional.

```bash
bunx shadcn@latest add @krak-stack/service-events
```

### Server

Provide the telemetry foundation and connect Events to browser ingestion:

```ts
import { BrowserCrypto } from '@effect/platform-browser';
import { Layer } from 'effect';
import { Events } from '@/services/events';
import { Otlp } from '@/services/opentelemetry';
import { HttpApiOtlp } from '@/services/opentelemetry/api';

const application = Events.layerWith({ requireConsent: true }).pipe(
  Layer.provide(BrowserCrypto.layer),
  Layer.provideMerge(Otlp.layer),
);

const server = HttpApiOtlp.layer.pipe(
  Layer.provide(Events.ingestionLayer),
  Layer.provideMerge(application),
);
```

Set `APP_SECRET` (stable, server-only, at least 32 characters), `VITE_SITE_URL` and your collector configuration:

```dotenv
OTEL_SERVICE_NAME=my-app-api
OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:4318
OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER=otlp
```

`Events.layerWith` accepts partial overrides for `origin`, `secret`, `serviceName`, `geolocation` and `requireConsent`. Missing origin/secret resolve from the environment. Service name otherwise comes from Otlp. Use distinct service names per environment.

### Browser

Mount this layer in your browser runtime, not during SSR:

```ts
import { Layer } from 'effect';
import { BrowserEvents } from '@/services/events/browser';
import { BrowserOtlp } from '@/services/opentelemetry/browser';

const browser = BrowserEvents.layer().pipe(
  Layer.provideMerge(BrowserOtlp.layer({ serviceName: 'my-app-web' })),
);
```

BrowserEvents requires acceptance by default. Mount the notice once in a persistent footer so visitors can choose and later change their preference.

## TrackingNotice

English/French defaults are included; no application message files are required.

```tsx
import { TrackingNotice } from '@/services/events/client/tracking-notice';

// Learn more opens the built-in dialog.
<TrackingNotice />

// Learn more links to your own policy instead.
<TrackingNotice privacyHref="/privacy-policy" />
```

Footer **Analytics preferences** always opens the consent controls, including when `privacyHref` is provided. There is no default KrakStack link.

### Locale

The component follows `KrakstackProvider`, with English fallback for unsupported languages:

```tsx
import { KrakstackProvider } from '@/components/ui/krakstack-provider';

<KrakstackProvider locale="fr" locales={['en', 'fr']}>
  <TrackingNotice privacyHref="/politique-de-confidentialite" />
</KrakstackProvider>

// Override the provider for one instance.
<TrackingNotice locale="fr" privacyHref="/politique-de-confidentialite" />
```

### Custom copy

Override only the messages you need. Use your application's translations for localized overrides.

```tsx
<TrackingNotice
  privacyHref="/privacy-policy"
  messages={{
    title: 'Help us understand opportunity interest',
    description:
      'With your permission, we record visits to public opportunity pages so organizations can understand interest in their postings.',
    learnMore: 'Learn how analytics works',
  }}
/>
```

Available keys: `preferences`, `title`, `description`, `learnMore`, `details`, `essential`, `privacy`, `accept`, `decline`, `close`, `blocked`, `accepted`, `declined`, `pending`, `error`. Match your copy to the tracking actually configured in your application.

## Tracking consent

| Feature, when configured | Accept | Decline / pending |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Page views and custom analytics events | On | Off |
| UTM campaigns, referrers, geography and device details | On | Off |
| Daily visitor IDs, visits and identified analytics | On | Off |
| Web Vitals | On | Off |
| Essential browser error reports | On | On |
| Necessary security/audit records and server diagnostics | On | On |

- **Accept:** records the current page without replaying earlier page views.
- **Decline, no choice or dismissal:** optional analytics stays off.
- **Saved choices:** remembered for 180 days in a first-party preference cookie; missing, invalid, expired or outdated-version preferences return to pending.
- **DNT/GPC:** overrides acceptance without replacing the saved choice. No signal does not mean consent.
- **Withdrawal:** stops new optional events; queued event records are checked before serialization. Already-started exports, including their retries, are not cancelled. Stored history is not automatically deleted.

DNT is an older do-not-track request; GPC is primarily a sale/sharing opt-out signal. The default policy treats either as a request to disable optional analytics. Server `Events` enforces this policy only with `requireConsent: true`, as shown in Setup; its legacy default is false. In that mode, request-scoped server analytics also requires acceptance, and analytics without an HTTP request is suppressed. Necessary audit events remain available.

The preference cookie stores choice, notice version, timestamps and a consent revision—not a visitor identity. Bump `ANALYTICS_NOTICE_VERSION` when renewed consent is needed. `requireConsent: false` is an explicit deployment override, not a compliance exemption.

### Cookieless does not mean anonymous

Analytics does not store visitor IDs in browser cookies or local storage. With trusted IP/browser information, the server can derive a daily-changing identifier: a limited form of fingerprinting. It is approximate, pseudonymous tracking. Daily rotation does not delete historical data or destroy the application secret used to derive it.

Your privacy policy should explain purposes, processors, retention and rights. Necessary diagnostics must not recreate declined analytics. Generic OTLP calls and third-party scripts are application-owned: gate or remove them separately. BrowserOtlp sanitizes automatic error messages and stack locations, but deployment logging and collector settings still need review. This is a product policy, not a legal-compliance guarantee. See [EDPB device-access guidance](https://www.edpb.europa.eu/documents/guideline/guidelines-22023-on-technical-scope-of-art-53-of-eprivacy-directive_en) and [CNIL audience-measurement guidance](https://www.cnil.fr/fr/cookies-solutions-pour-les-outils-de-mesure-daudience).

## Browser events

Run these Effects in the mounted browser runtime:

```ts
BrowserEvents.track('download.started', { format: 'pdf' });
BrowserEvents.page({ path: '/opportunities', name: 'Opportunities' });
```

| Layer option | Default / behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `requireConsent` | true; require shared acceptance |
| `respectDoNotTrack` | true; honor DNT/GPC; shared consent also honors them |
| `pageViews` | true; initial and SPA pathname views |
| `enabled` | true; false disables BrowserEvents, not other telemetry |
| `locale` | Optional locale callback |
| `sanitizePath` | Replace personal path segments with route templates |

Properties become `app.*` attributes. Browser identity and audit claims are discarded. BrowserOtlp owns shared batching (30 seconds / 100 events by default); configure `events` on BrowserOtlp to adjust it.

## Storage and delivery

Without SQL, events are enriched and forwarded to your collector. The collector owns storage and retention; delivery is best effort.

To enable application-owned history, provide a PostgreSQL or SQLite `SqlClient` to Events:

```ts
import { PgClient } from '@effect/sql-pg';
import { Config } from 'effect';

const sqlLayer = PgClient.layerConfig({ url: Config.Redacted('DATABASE_URL') });
const application = Events.layerWith({ requireConsent: true }).pipe(
  Layer.provide(sqlLayer),
  Layer.provide(BrowserCrypto.layer),
  Layer.provideMerge(Otlp.layer),
);
```

`Events.layer` / `layerWith` run migrations; `baseLayer` / `baseLayerWith` leave migrations to the application. Keep the same SqlClient available to services that share transactions.

| Table | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `events` | Indexed event/identity/time fields and complete OTLP `payload_json` |
| `events_migrations` | Migration history |

SQL is authoritative: failed writes fail recording. Successful new inserts emit to OTLP; duplicates do not. Forwarding failure does not undo committed browser analytics. There is no outbox or atomic SQL/OTLP delivery; a server event queued inside an outer transaction cannot be recalled if that transaction later rolls back.

## Server events and audit

Use `Otlp.event` for collector-only telemetry. Use `Events.track` for optional SQL recording and audit validation:

```ts
const events = yield* Events;
yield* events.track({
  eventId: `document:${requestId}:deleted`,
  name: 'document.deleted',
  category: 'audit',
  target: { id: documentId, name: documentName, type: 'document' },
});
```

Audit events require verified `app.actor.type/id` annotations and a typed target. Auth supplies actor and authentication context; do not trust browser-supplied identity. `track` returns `{ eventId, inserted }`; without SQL, `inserted` is false even when telemetry is emitted. Suppressed analytics also returns false without emission.

| Context | Attributes |
| --- | --- |
| Responsible principal | `app.actor.type`, `app.actor.id` |
| Authentication | `app.auth.method` (`session` / `api_key`), `app.auth.credential.id` |
| User / tenant | `user.id`, `user.roles`, `organization.id` |
| Audit user snapshot | `user.full_name`, `user.name`, `user.email` |
| Audit target | `app.audit.target.id/name/type` |

Verified request annotations replace explicit fallback identity as a whole. For analytics ingestion, provide AuthMiddleware on `/api/otel/v1/logs` or supply an `identity(request)` Effect returning verified user/organization IDs or null. Resolver failures fail ingestion, rather than silently making events anonymous. Authorization remains application-owned. A key identifies its principal, not whether a human, agent or CLI operated it. Avoid sensitive target names/properties.

SQL deduplicates by `(service_name, source, event_id)`. Reusing an ID with the same caller-owned content returns `inserted: false`; different content raises `EventConflictError`. Supply stable IDs for retryable operations.

## AuditLogTable

Authorize tenant access before querying and fix the category server-side:

```tsx
const page = yield* events.list({
  organizationId,
  category: 'audit',
  page: 0,
  pageSize: 20,
  eventName: 'document.deleted',
  globalFilter: 'document',
  sort: [{ id: 'time', direction: 'desc' }],
});

<AuditLogTable
  events={[{ value: 'document.deleted', label: m.document_deleted() }]}
  entries={page.data}
  rowCount={page.meta.total}
  state={query}
  onStateChange={setQuery}
/>
```

`list` replaces `listAudit` and requires SQL, an organization ID and an explicit `audit` or `analytics` category. Results are scoped to the configured service and requested organization. Audit queries include only server-originated records; analytics queries include matching browser and server records. Filtering, sorting and pagination happen on the server. The optional `eventName` filter is an exact, case-sensitive match, combined with category and search before counting and pagination. The response contains unchanged EventLogRecord values plus pagination metadata. Sort IDs: `time`, `eventName`, `recordType`, `record`, `actorType`, `actorId`.

Use `EventQuery` from `/events/schema` for API query schemas and client atom types, and `EventQueryStandard` for route search validation. Both extend the shared table query with `eventName`. Keep that query through the entire API/client/route path so the selected action survives other table changes.

Pass the full application-owned event catalog through `events`, not just event names from the current page. Each option has an exact `value` and a localized `label`; supply labels from your application's translations. Controlled tables show an **Action** dropdown with a filter icon as the first toolbar menu. Selecting an option sets `eventName` and resets the page to zero; **All actions** clears it. The same labels appear in the Action column, with raw event names as fallback. A custom `renderAction` takes precedence.

The table displays Time, Action, Target, Actor and Method. User labels come from the recorded OpenTelemetry `user.full_name`, `user.name` and `user.email` attributes, with email or ID as secondary text. No Auth lookup, identity link or separate actors prop is needed. Missing snapshots retain neutral labels and recorded IDs. Trusted server name/email annotations are preserved for audit events and omitted from analytics; apply appropriate access and retention controls for personal data. Target names are also event-time snapshots: record a readable `target.name` when tracking the action. The Target column displays that name with type and ID as secondary text. When a name is missing or duplicates the ID, it shows the target type above the ID instead. Existing events are not backfilled or resolved against current entities. Method reads recorded authentication context, not inferred browser/operator information. Locale follows KrakstackProvider. The dateTime column defaults to `America/New_York`; override it with `timeZone`. Use locale-keyed `messages`, `renderAction`, `loading` and `error` for customization.

### Migration

Replace `Events.listAudit` / `ListAudit` with `Events.list` / `ListEvents` and explicitly fix `category: 'audit'` in audit handlers. Remove `AuditActor`, the `actors` prop and browser profile lookups. Use `EventQuery` / `EventQueryStandard` instead of the generic query schemas where action filtering is needed, and supply the labeled `events` catalog.

## Geography and visits

Geolocation is off by default. Configure `geolocation: 'cloudflare'` only behind trusted Cloudflare ingress with origin-bypass protection, or supply an Effect lookup returning validated IP/country/region/city fields. Raw IP/UA are not automatically persisted.

With SQL and trusted IP/UA, events share a visit within a 30-minute inactivity window. Daily visitor rotation splits new visits at UTC midnight; retries retain their original visit. Scope queries by service and verified tenant/user. Retain at least 30 minutes of event history if deriving visits.

## Web Vitals

```ts
import { BrowserWebVitals } from '@/services/opentelemetry/web-vitals';

const browser = Layer.mergeAll(
  BrowserEvents.layer(),
  BrowserWebVitals.layer(),
).pipe(Layer.provideMerge(telemetry));
```

Web Vitals requires acceptance before the page loads. Late acceptance starts it on the next full page load; withdrawal keeps it off for the rest of the current document. It uses the shared exporter and generic OTLP scope, without Events SQL storage. See [OpenTelemetry](./service-opentelemetry) for metrics and transport options.

## Package imports and limits

Package consumers use `@krak-stack/registry/events`, `/events/browser`, `/events/tracking-notice`, `/events/client` (AuditLogTable), `/events/schema`, `/events/record` and `/events/migrations`. Otlp lives at `/opentelemetry`.

Browser ingestion uses `/api/otel/v1/logs`, JSON batches up to 64 KiB / 100 application records, matching Origin, and timestamps from the previous hour through one minute ahead. Generic events remain separate from the `krakstack.application.events` scope. Apply edge rate limits, permissions, retention and backups; avoid personal data and high-cardinality metric/Loki labels.
